what_happened.line: Two members of the Council on Aging agreed to draft a petition to state delegations and Mart about rides to Worcester hospitals, for the next meeting.
The board discussed the two special town meeting articles that night: an appropriation for Mart Connect, and a revolving fund for the meal site.
The Mart Connect article was described as needed because the grant that funded the program expired; the program is not guaranteed past the grant period.
The director presented FY24 and FY23 usage and funding figures, and a member worked out the municipal budget per user as roughly a dollar a day per visit.
A Sunshine fund for cards to seniors in need was moved and seconded, but the outcome of the vote is not audible; a member volunteered to lead it.

why_it_matters: Residents who use or may use the senior van to reach Worcester hospitals have a stake in the Mart Connect article, since it moves money from the overlay surplus account to replace an expired grant.
The meal-site revolving fund would let the kitchen buy food with its own receipts, which touches how a senior meal program is paid for outside the regular budget.
watch_next: The petition on Worcester rides, due at the next Council on Aging meeting.
The state formula grant annual report, which has not arrived and holds up the FY26 Council on Aging budget request.
